page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.8 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU features a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES instructions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate single-core capabilities but constrained multi-core and memory throughput. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls in the average category at 1827.69, whereas the multi-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% at 1875.88. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also register in the bottom 10%, with read-only large block speeds at 13.86 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.77 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET performance of 1.67 million operations per second rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the physical limitations of the 2-vCPU hardware envelope.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated Intel Xeon resources with a high memory-to-core ratio. It is designed for workloads that require more memory capacity than compute power but do not demand high parallel processing capabilities. Suitable workloads include small-scale databases, lightweight caching layers, basic web serving, and memory-sensitive background processes that do not heavily stress the CPU.
